1#א: Whether whole, etc. Language of the Tur — meaning: not only when whole, according to the tanna of a litra of pressed figs, which otherwise would not be nullified, as stated above siman 86 seif 3; but even when beaten, and like water and salt in dough (Beitzah 39a) — there.
1#ב: And even if there is doubt, etc. Gemara there.
1#ג: And it was mixed, etc. Tur; and as Mordechai wrote in seif 3 of Avodah Zarah, and he derived from this that a double doubt is forbidden regarding something that has a permitted aspect; and as stated above siman 110 seif 8 in the hagahah; and Rosh in responsum part 7 of Avodah Zarah wrote that a double doubt helps; and all the more so in siman 293 seif 3 in the hagahah — only because of one doubt in the mixture — see there beginning general rule 2; and it depends on the dispute in siman 110 seif 9 in Shulchan Aruch and hagahah; and not like Rashba who wrote "and if it was mixed" refers to certainty specifically; but in Orach Chayim siman 513 stam, like the opinion of Rashba.
1#ד: And if it was mixed, etc. As written in Nedarim 58a — everything that has a permitted aspect, such as tevel, etc.; and we say in chapter 3 of Challah that tevel forbids, etc.; and there 52a regarding one who vowed, etc. — even though it is something that has a permitted aspect; and as written there 59a; and so in Yerushalmi there; and we learn from this: this general rule was Rashba's because of R' Yehoshua — everything that has a permitted aspect, such as tevel; and what he wrote regarding hekdesh and chadash — the Sages did not give a measure except in its kind in any amount and not in its kind in sixty; and everything that has no permitted aspect, such as terumah, etc. — these vows, what do you do with them? As something that has a permitted aspect or as something that has no permitted aspect? Reasonably we act as something that has a permitted aspect, for we learned there that the elder uproots the vow from its root, etc.; and this Mishnah does for them as something that has no permitted aspect, for we learned that one who vowed from a matter and it was mixed — if there is sixty in it, it is forbidden; resolve in its kind, not in its kind; and Tosafot chapter 5 of Yevamot 38a s.v. "and let it be nullified," etc.; and one can say, etc.
1#ה: However, etc. Tosafot there 38a s.v. "because," etc.; and one can say, etc.
1#ו: And in Orach Chayim, etc. There seif 3 — anything for appearance, etc. — meaning: everything that comes to fix, whether for appearance or for taste, is as in its kind; but on account of appearance without something that has a permitted aspect it does not forbid; and Rashi in Zevachim 74a s.v. "and where," etc.; and even though they raised a doubt in Bava Kamma 101a whether appearance is significant and it was not resolved — poskim ruled it is a doubt, as Shulchan Aruch Choshen Mishpat end of seif 363; and there Rava distinguishes between d'oraisa and d'rabbanan — it appears that d'oraisa appearance is significant, and all the more so for R' Yochanan in Niddah 62b — one can say even d'rabbanan; and Tosafot there s.v. "from leniencies," etc.; nevertheless all this is in prohibition of benefit; and as written there "benefit that is visible," etc. — appearance helps, unlike Peri Chadash who erred here in all this.
2#א: There are those who say, etc. Only, etc. — meaning: to exclude a doubtful tereifah egg, for even though it is possible the chicken will lay eggs or live, it is not certain; and as written below "therefore egg," etc.; and as written at the beginning of Yom Tov 3b "if not, doubtful tereifah," etc.; and even according to Rashi's explanation there — what is the challenge? It should have said "born from doubtful tereifah."
2#ב: Or if, etc. Tosafot Bava Metzia 53a s.v. "to return"; and on this 53b s.v. "tevel," etc.: (Excerpt) Without loss. Tosafot Bava Metzia 53a s.v. "to return," etc.; but Rashi there did not explain so — see there s.v. "and they ascend," etc.; and here such as, etc.; and there is not, etc. (end).
3#_: (Excerpt) Vessel, etc. See what is written in siman 122 seif 8 (end).
4#א: There are those who say, etc. As above seif 2 — or, etc. — without loss.
4#ב: That something that has a permitted aspect, etc. Like an egg and the like: (Excerpt) That something that has a permitted aspect, etc. Hagahot Alfasi chapter 5 of Avodah Zarah 69 s.v. something that has a permitted aspect, etc. (end).
4#ג: Or that there is, etc. Like water and salt.
4#ד: But, etc. As written at the beginning of Yom Tov 4b — this applies where it is in prohibition in existence, etc.; and therefore it was reasonable what they needed in Avodah Zarah 73b to say on tevel (in any amount) because of "like its permission," etc. — namely leaven that fell and was removed; but since Tosafot there s.v. "tevel" needed to resolve another matter, it does not appear so; and likewise in seif 3 "a vessel that became forbidden," etc.; and so too Peri Chadash.
4#ה: And likewise if there is not, etc. All the Acharonim disagree on this — and Taz and Shach: (Excerpt) And likewise if, etc. Like a piece worthy of honor in siman 101 seif 2 (end). (Excerpt) And likewise if there is not, etc. — meaning: if the matter is not absorbed from its kind; and as Tosafot wrote there (in siman 101 s.k. 7) (end).
4#ו: Even though some say, etc. This is the opinion of Rif in chapter 3 of Forbidden Foods who ruled "all of it" in Pesachim 76b; and even though Rav Kahana taught, etc. — that flask, etc. — that "all of it" also comes because it is something that has a permitted aspect, for it is possible to eat alone and with a Jew and a little scent — nevertheless it is so; and as written in Orach Chayim siman 447 seif 1 in the hagahah — and some are stringent, etc.; and Mordechai there in the name of Rabeinu Yehudah seized on this from that which chapter of Orlah (Yevamot chapter 2 1a) — and that which Rav Ashi, etc.; and likewise here with meat it was never forbidden; and Ran in Nedarim 52a resolved: some say for its name, since it is permitted for everyone; and above siman 108 seif 1 in the hagahah ruled not like Rif who wrote "and if one baked bread with meat," etc. — permitted in both, for this, etc.; and like the first reason Rif wrote there that "all of it" is permitted only b'dieved.
4#ז: Every prohibition, etc. As written in Orach Chayim siman 318 seif 2: (Excerpt) Every prohibition, etc. From that which Bava Kamma seif 9 (1); and see there Tosafot s.v. "everything," etc.; and even though something that has a permitted aspect, etc.; and according to what is written here it is reasonable; and see what is written in Orach Chayim siman 320 seif 2 (end).
4#ח: One who vowed, etc. As written in Yerushalmi chapter 6 of Nedarim and as stated above.
4#ט: For, etc. There and in the Gemara 59a.
4#י: Something, etc. such as, etc. From what is written in Avodah Zarah 74a — let it also teach chametz on Pesach; and if so, it would forbid anyway on account of something that has a permitted aspect; and there it excludes, etc.
4#כ: And there are those who disagree. As Ran wrote — this is because he holds like R' Yehudah that chametz after Pesach is forbidden from the Torah; but we, who hold like R' Shimon, it is something that has a permitted aspect; and this is what Rava said in Pesachim 30a "Rabbi, the halachah: chametz," etc. — even though he does not hold like Rav that in its kind in any amount, but because it is something that has a permitted aspect; Rava according to his reason holds like R' Shimon as written there; and Rav needed to say on account of in its kind in any amount because he holds after Pesach like R' Yehudah as written there; and this is what Rambam wrote that the reason for chametz in any amount is because it is something that has a permitted aspect; but from R' Yochanan there it is difficult, for he holds like R' Shimon after its time, and nevertheless he holds in its time even in its kind in sixty — one must say R' Yochanan and Rava dispute in this (whether this is called something that has a permitted aspect, and we hold like Rava). But the first reasoning holds as Tosafot wrote there on account of the severity of chametz, etc. — see there s.v. "he said," etc.; and Orach Chayim siman 447 seif 2 stam like the first reasoning, and as Maggid Mishneh wrote (chapter 1 of Laws of Chametz law 5) that for Rambam even by taste in any amount — see there seif 9: (Excerpt) And there are those who disagree. As Rava said Pesachim 30a; and even though he holds all Torah prohibitions in sixty, as in Pesachim (57b) — from Rav it is not difficult that Rav needed to say according to his reasoning, because Rav holds like R' Yehudah after its time, and likewise Shmuel for clarity of the matter even like R' Yehudah; and this is what he said "not in its time," etc. like R' Shimon; but in its time, even for R' Yehudah and R' Yochanan one can say he holds like the rabbis who argue on R' Shimon — for that which is something that has a permitted aspect is R' Shimon's, and the rabbis argue on him (see in Sefer HaEshkol); and this is what is written in Avodah Zarah 73b "thus R' Yehudah," etc.; and Tosafot there s.v. "tevel," etc. — and one might ask, etc.; and therefore it comes according to the rabbis, and so they said there R' Yehudah, meaning except tevel, etc. [see Milchamot chapter Kamma] — and it appears specifically tevel; and if so, all that has a permitted aspect is likewise — and he says above "granted," etc. (end).
4#ל: And not, etc. As above (s.k. 15) from chapter Orlah.
